title: Response lifecycle cost lab notes
content:
Purpose and context

Working notes for a first-cut UX + wireframe iteration: a dashboard that surfaces the full 'response lifecycle' for an invocation, with token-level cost and latency attribution. This doc captures hypotheses, sketches, data needs, and a prioritized backlog of small-ish UX experiments we can ship in the console. Iteration intent: give engineers quick signal for why a specific invocation was expensive/slow and where optimizations (batching, cache, truncation, model variant) will have the biggest impact.

Audience
- Platform engineers debugging production regressions
- App developers optimizing per-invocation cost/latency of LLM calls
- SREs looking for patterns for autoscale/fallback thresholds

High level goals (MVP)
1) Surface a single-invocation waterfall view: tokens across request/response timeline, with per-token cost and latency bars.
2) Provide simple root-cause suggestions (e.g., "prefix repeated 250 tokens -> enable prefix cache") and quick actions (pin model variant, change batching policy).
3) Make aggregation easy: slice by route/model/prompt-template and surface common expensive token patterns.

User scenarios
- "Why did this customer call cost $0.42?" -> open invocation, see token breakdown, identify >60% cost from streaming completion tokens, suggest truncation or more aggressive stop sequences.
- "We have increased tail latency after rollout" -> sample invocations, see higher per-token kernel time on long sequences; surface which model variant and sequence length buckets drive the regression.
- "I want a lightweight investigator for async jobs that run at scale" -> aggregated heatmap view of token cost vs latency by bucket (seq len, model, geo).

Wireframe notes (rough sketch to implement in Figma)
- Header: invocation metadata (invocation id, timestamp, route, model, variant, region, status, total tokens, total cost, total latency). Small action row: [Pin variant] [Re-run with debug flags] [Open raw payload].

- Main panel (left): Response lifecycle waterfall (time on x-axis). Rows: request tokens (prefix + prompt), server-kernel time per token, network/streaming time per chunk, KV cache hits highlighted, response tokens. Visuals: stacked bars with color legend (compute, kv-cache, batching-delay, network). Hover shows token text snippet, cost cents, latency ms, kernel name (e.g., fwd-attn-opt-v3).

- Token table (right): compact scrollable list of tokens in order with columns: position, token_text (truncated), token_type (prompt/response/prefix/cache-hit), compute_ms, stream_ms, cents, kernel_tag, kv_hit_bool, notes. Click token -> center timeline on that token and expand neighboring tokens.

- Bottom panel: heuristics + recommended actions. Card list with simple heuristics and confidence: e.g.,
  * "Repeated prefix detected (250 repeated tokens) — enable prefix cache -> EST SAVING 0.15$ / invoc"
  * "High streaming delays due to many small chunks — recommend rebatch/streaming buffer"
  * "Model selection: x-quant vs x-fp16 tradeoff: lower cost but +12% median latency"
Each card has [Try fix] which triggers a guided repro run on a sandbox variant (dev only).

- Aggregation toggle: "Investigate similar invocations" -> shows small multiples of waterfalls grouped by slice (same route, same 95th percentile seq len). Click group -> show cluster summary and representative invocation.

Interaction details / microcopy
- Hover token: show token text on left with surrounding 8-token context and two quick links: [Highlight all same-token-occurrences] [Mark as noise].
- When kernel tag shown, provide tooltip: kernel tag -> quick explanation and link to infra doc (e.g., "kv-cache-on-quantized-kernel: optimized for seq<1024").
- Confidence badges on recommendations: low/medium/high with short explanation: "High — deterministic pattern: repeated prefix >50 occurrences".

Data model & backend requirements (MVP)
- Required per-invocation trace: token list (ordered), per-token timings (compute_ms, stream_ms), cost attribution (micro-cents), kernel_tag, kv_hit boolean, chunk id for streaming, model_variant id, route id.
- Retention: keep full token-level traces for 30 days for in-console investigation. Aggregate summaries (profiles) for 12 months.
- Sampling: default full traces for failed/high-cost invocations; sampled traces for normal traffic (1 in 1000) to keep volume manageable.
- API: GET /invocations/{id}/lifecycle -> returns sequence-aligned arrays (note: arrays only — aligns with console needs). We need an evictable S3-backed blob store for heavy traces.

Performance considerations
- Rendering: avoid showing >2000 tokens at once in UI; clamp and encourage 'zoom to window'. Pagination should be token-range based, not page-number, for smooth timeline panning.
- Data transfer: compress token traces server-side; client decompress and progressively render.
- Security: traces can contain user prompt text — only surface to users with appropriate view permissions; mask tokens in public-shared links.

Backlog (prioritized)
1) P0: Single-invocation waterfall + token table + header metadata. Acceptance: developers can open an invocation and see per-token cost & compute time. (JIRA-REQ-2001)
2) P0: Heuristics engine basic rules (prefix repeat, KV hits dominance, excessive small-stream chunks). Acceptance: top-3 heuristics surfaced with estimated dollar savings or latency reduction. (JIRA-REQ-2002)
3) P1: Aggregation buckets + representative invocation sampling. Acceptance: group view shows clusters by route and seq len. (JIRA-REQ-2010)
4) P1: Quick action: re-run on sandbox variant, pin variant rollout. (JIRA-REQ-2012)
5) P2: Kernel tag linkouts and infra glossary integration.
6) P2: Export trace to CSV/psuedo-llm for downstream analysis.

Open questions / design tradeoffs
- How much of the raw token text are we allowed to persist for enterprise customers with strict data controls? For Private deployments this is admin-configurable via retention policies, but default for hosted should be opt-in. (Action: sync with security-compliance).
- How to show uncertainty in cost attribution for shared kernels or batched compute? E.g., if compute time is for a batched kernel, per-token split is an estimate. Recommendation: show "estimated" tag and provide math + sampling documentation.
- Sampling heuristics: how many full traces before we stop sampling? We need product signal for common customers to decide thresholds. (Action: propose defaults: full trace if cost > $0.25 or latency > 3s or status != 200).

Low-fidelity wireframe checklist for designers
- Export CSV of token table for developers (include kernel_tag + hex-token-index)
- Storyboard: open invocation -> see waterfall -> click heuristic -> try fix -> repro on sandbox -> monitor diff.
- Visual legend for cost vs latency (use separate color palettes to keep accessibility).
- Mobile considerations: waterfall collapses to condensed stacked bars + token table hidden behind toggle.

Acceptance criteria (MVP P0)
- Console lists invocation metadata with correct totals (tokens/cost/latency).
- Timeline renders per-token bars and token table rows for a 512-token invocation within 1.2s client-side on a standard Core i5 laptop.
- Top-3 heuristics appear for >60% of flagged invocations and match infra-detected conditions.

Next steps / owners
- Designer: Maya Singh -> produce 3 wireframe variations in Figma by 2025-11-01.
- Infra: Jonah Park -> prototype lifecycle API + storage design by 2025-11-08.
- Product: Avery Chen -> sync with security/compliance and compile retention policy decision doc by 2025-11-05.
- SRE: Diego Rivera -> define sampling rules and threshold defaults by 2025-11-10.

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally exploratory: please call out missing heuristics you rely on when debugging cost/latency issues. Add examples of invocations (anonymized) to the Figma comments so we can validate wireframes against real traces.

Quick proto checklist for engineering spike (2w)
- Minimal API to fetch a single invocation lifecycle JSON (Jonah)
- Simple React canvas to draw token bars with hover (MVP using pre-sampled static JSON) (Frontend)
- Basic heuristics module (rule-based, configurable) that runs on fetched trace and returns recommendations with confidence (Backend)

References and inspiration
- Existing internal token-inspector prototypes (see figma link)
- External: "profiling web requests with flame graphs" blog — adapted for token timelines.

TODOs / outstanding
- Confirm data retention defaults with legal (Avery)
- Put together cost modeling for recommendations (how we estimate $ saved) (Maya + Infra)
